question.knowledge_point: Finding a Quadratic Polynomial Given Two Imaginary or Complex Roots
question.problem: The quadratic polynomial $f(z)$ has real coefficients, has roots ${z}_{1}=3+2\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=3-2\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $-2.$ Find $f(z).$
question.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${z}_{1}=3+2\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=3-2\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(z-{z}_{1})(z-{z}_{2}) & =(-2)(z-(3+2\text{i}))(z-(3-2\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(-2)(z-(3+2\text{i}))(z-(3-2\text{i})) & =(-2)({z}^{2}-(3+2\text{i})z-(3-2\text{i})z+(3+2\text{i})(3-2\text{i})) \\  & =(-2)({z}^{2}-(3+2\text{i}+3-2\text{i})z+({3}^{2}-{2}^{2}{\text{i}}^{2})) \\  & =(-2)({z}^{2}-6z+(9+4)) \\  & =-2{z}^{2}+12z-26.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(z)=-2{z}^{2}+12z-26.$
